_source.description: Major global phosphate rock mining and production sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); USGS Mineral Resources Data System (https://mrdata.usgs.gov/mrds/); International Fertilizer Association (IFA) (https://www.ifastat.org/); S&P Global Market Intelligence; Company annual reports: OCP Group (Morocco), Mosaic Company, Nutrien, PhosAgro, Ma'aden/SABIC, JPMC, ICL Group, CMOC Group, Foskor, CPG (Tunisia), ICS/Indorama (Senegal), SNPT (Togo), El-Nasr Mining (Egypt), Itafos, Ferphos/Somiphos (Algeria)
_source.license: USGS: public domain; IFA: summary data fair use; OCP/company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Major phosphate rock mining operations globally. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Capacity figures in phosphate rock tonnes per annum. Morocco (OCP Group) holds over 70% of world reserves. Phosphate rock is the primary feedstock for phosphoric acid and fertilizer production.

_coverage.global_production_source: USGS MCS 2024 — ~220 million tonnes phosphate rock
_coverage.known_gaps: Smaller Chinese phosphate operations across Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, and Hubei; smaller Russian phosphate mines; Vietnamese phosphate operations; North Korean Musan-area deposits; numerous small-scale operations in sub-Saharan Africa

sites.name: Khouribga
sites.notes: World's largest phosphate mining complex; Oulad Abdoun basin; multiple open-pit mines including Merah el Aharch, Sidi Daoui, Sidi Chennane

sites.name: Benguerir
sites.notes: Gantour basin mining complex; includes OCP's Mohammed VI Polytechnic University campus and green energy research

sites.name: Youssoufia
sites.notes: Gantour basin; one of Morocco's original phosphate mining centers; underground and open-pit operations

sites.name: Bou Craa
sites.notes: Open-pit mine with 100km conveyor belt to Laayoune port; sovereignty disputed between Morocco and Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic

sites.name: Guizhou phosphate complex (Wengfu)
sites.notes: China's largest phosphate producer; integrated mine-to-fertilizer complex in Guizhou province; Kaiyang district

sites.name: Yunnan phosphate complex (Yuntianhua)
sites.notes: Major integrated phosphate-fertilizer complex; Kunming area; includes Haikou, Jinning, Anning mining operations

sites.name: Hubei phosphate complex (Xingfa)
sites.notes: Yichang area, Hubei province; integrated phosphate mining and phosphorus chemical production

sites.name: Sichuan phosphate operations
sites.ownership: Multiple Chinese state and private operators
sites.notes: Mianzhu and Shifang districts near Deyang, Sichuan; multiple mines feeding integrated chemical complexes

sites.name: South Fort Meade
sites.notes: Central Florida phosphate district; large-scale dragline strip mining; feeds Mosaic's New Wales chemical plant

sites.name: Four Corners
sites.notes: Central Florida Bone Valley; adjacent operations to South Fort Meade; dragline surface mining

sites.name: Riverview
sites.notes: Major phosphoric acid and fertilizer production complex; Hillsborough County, Florida; processes Florida phosphate rock

sites.name: White Springs (Swift Creek / Suwannee River)
sites.notes: North Florida phosphate operation; Hamilton County; Nutrien's only US phosphate mining operation

sites.name: Aurora (PCS Phosphate)
sites.notes: Largest integrated phosphate mining and chemical complex in the US; Beaufort County, North Carolina

sites.name: Caldwell Canyon / Rasmussen Ridge
sites.notes: Southeastern Idaho Phosphate Resource Area (SEIPRA); Caribou County; Western US phosphate district

sites.name: Conda/Smoky Canyon
sites.notes: Caribou County, Idaho; integrated mine and acid plant; one of few remaining Western US phosphate operations

sites.name: Kirovsk / Apatity (Apatit)
sites.notes: World's largest apatite mining complex; Khibiny Mountains, Kola Peninsula; multiple underground and open-pit mines; operating since 1929

sites.name: Voskresensk
sites.notes: Major phosphoric acid and fertilizer production complex; Moscow region; processes Kola Peninsula apatite concentrate

sites.name: Balakovo
sites.notes: Major fertilizer production complex; Saratov Oblast; one of PhosAgro's largest downstream plants

sites.name: Al Hasa (Eshidiya South)
sites.ownership: JPMC (Brunei Investment Agency 37%, Government of Jordan ~25%)
sites.notes: Al Hasa and surrounding mines in southern Jordan; JPMC is world's 6th largest phosphate producer

sites.name: Eshidiya
sites.notes: Largest phosphate mine in Jordan; Ma'an Governorate; open-pit mining; railway to Aqaba port for export

sites.name: Al Jalamid (Wa'ad Al Shamal)
sites.notes: Wa'ad Al Shamal Phosphate Company; integrated mine-to-DAP complex in Northern Border Province; world-class scale facility commissioned 2016

sites.name: Negev (Rotem/Zin)
sites.notes: Negev Desert operations including Rotem, Zin, and Oron mines; ICL is also major Dead Sea minerals producer

sites.name: Tapira
sites.notes: Alkaline-carbonatite intrusion in Minas Gerais; part of Alto Paranaiba Igneous Province

sites.name: Catalao
sites.ownership: CMOC Group (100%, acquired from Anglo American 2016)
sites.notes: Goias state; integrated phosphate-niobium complex; weathered carbonatite; CMOC (China Molybdenum Co.)

sites.name: Araxa
sites.notes: Barreiro carbonatite complex in Minas Gerais; integrated mining and chemical processing; adjacent to CBMM niobium mine

sites.name: Bayovar (Miski Mayo)
sites.notes: Sechura Desert, Piura region; one of world's largest phosphate deposits; open-pit mining; exported to Brazil and Asia

sites.name: Abu Tartur
sites.notes: New Valley Governorate (Western Desert); one of Egypt's major phosphate operations; railway to Nile Valley

sites.name: Red Sea coast (Safaga/Quseir)
sites.notes: Multiple mines along Red Sea mountains corridor; Quseir, Safaga, and Hamrawein operations; Eastern Desert

sites.name: Gafsa basin
sites.notes: Historic mining basin with multiple mines (Metlaoui, Redeyef, M'Dhilla); operating since 1899; production disrupted by social unrest since 2011

sites.name: Djebel Onk
sites.notes: Tebessa province, eastern Algeria near Tunisian border; open-pit mining; significant reserves for future expansion

sites.name: Taiba / Lam-Lam
sites.notes: Thies region; high-grade Eocene phosphorite; ICS is West Africa's largest phosphoric acid producer; Indian-owned

sites.name: Hahotoe / Kpogame
sites.operator: SNPT (Societe Nouvelle des Phosphates du Togo)
sites.ownership: Government of Togo / Wengfu Group (management contract)
sites.notes: Maritime Region; coastal phosphate deposits; Chinese (Wengfu) management since 2007; historically important export commodity for Togo

sites.name: Phalaborwa
sites.ownership: Government of South Africa (IDC, 58%), other shareholders
sites.notes: Palabora igneous complex, Limpopo province; open-pit apatite-magnetite mining; adjacent to Kruger National Park; integrated mine-acid plant

sites.name: Bourem / Tilemsi
sites.notes: Tilemsi Valley phosphate deposits; significant undeveloped resources; security situation limits development in northern Mali

sites.name: Minjingu
sites.notes: Near Lake Manyara; small-scale operation producing direct-application phosphate rock for East African agriculture

sites.name: Jhamarkotra / Udaipur
sites.notes: Rajasthan; India's largest phosphate rock mining complex; Jhamarkotra and surrounding deposits; low-grade requires beneficiation

sites.name: Mussorie / Dehradun
sites.ownership: Government of India (Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers)
sites.notes: Uttarakhand; low-grade Precambrian-Cambrian phosphorite; India exploring to reduce import dependence
